title: Field catalyst: regional model compatibility probing and vendor signal synthesis
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: run a compact, reproducible field lab that evaluates candidate open and hosted models across regional constraints (NA, EU) and produces a vendor-signal synthesis and a compatibility rubric the procurement and sales teams can use.

Why now: increasing buyer scrutiny around regional latency, data residency, and fallback readiness means we must translate low-level telemetry into procurement triggers (e.g., switch candidate, reserved capacity request, or canary routing rules). Current competitive scans list many model entrants but lack operational compatibility signals (KV cache behavior, quantization regressions, cold-start jitter).

Deliverables: 
- Compatibility scoring rubric (latency buckets, reliability, quantization resilience, API/parity, tooling integrations).
- Pilot matrix: 12 model variants across 3 regions under 4 synthetic workload profiles.
- Vendor signal dossier: per-vendor notes, likely mitigation paths, and suggested routing/policy actions.
- Instrumentation checklist and required telemetry (ENG tickets).
- Short playbook: procurement trigger thresholds and example runbooks for switching/fallback.

Scope & success metrics:
- Complete pilot runs in NA and EU with baseline telemetry captured (latency P50/P95/P99, tokens/sec, cold-start ms, KV cache hit rate) by 2025-02-14.
- Produce rubric that maps to a binary decision: Fallback-ready | Needs Reserved | Blocker.
- Reduce model-deprecation procurement lead time estimate by 30% (tracked by PM-772345).

Signals to capture (agreed with ENG 2025-01-22):
- End-to-end cold-start latency (ms) under warm and cold cache conditions.
- Per-token latency distribution and P99/P999 tail behavior under continuous batching.
- Quantized variant semantic regression rate on a 200-case prompt set (quality delta).
- KV cache miss amplification (how much cost/latency increases when cache misses occur).
- API parity gaps (structured output / function-calling quirks).
- Operational failure types and SLO breach modes (timeouts, OOM, degraded responses).

Trade-offs and constraints noted:
- We will limit to 12 model variants to keep budget and runtime manageable; not every vendor invited. Selection prioritizes enterprise-signaled entrants and those with known quantized builds.
- Some hosted vendors restrict regional testing; for those we will simulate via latency injection where allowed but mark as 'synthetic' in dossier.
- Quality regressions sometimes depend on prompt engineering; we will use a curated 200-prompt probe that reflects real customer intents (search summarization, RAG summarization, code-extraction).

Next actions: 
- ENG (Evan Chen) to land telemetry hooks and create ENG-5821 (telemetry) — blockers: trace propagation for multi-hop batching.
- Research (Sofia Martinez) to finalize 200-prompt probe and baseline expected outputs; deliverable: probe CSV in Drive.
- PM (Marcus) to prepare vendor outreach notes and schedule 1:1 with top 6 vendors for test access.

Risks: 
- Vendor non-cooperation could force synthetic testing; we label those entries.
- Telemetry variance across infra makes cross-region comparability harder; will normalize by injecting controlled load and repeating runs.

Attachment notes: Confluence spec contains rubric template; Drive has prompt probes and raw results; Grafana dashboards will be created under "Model Sourcing Lab" stack.

Stakeholders: procurement, solutions engineering, dedicated-ops, privacy (for regional residency considerations).
